name: DarkGEO
summary: An independent successor proposal to convert the existing GEO600 facility into a large laser axion detector in stages.
detection_principle: A long optical path and precision polarization interferometry enhance axion-field birefringence, with multiple readout channels testing consistency.

status.label: Public proposal / conceptual design
status.evidence: 2024 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: DarkGEO: A Large-Scale Laser-Interferometric Axion Detector

collaboration.name: DarkGEO Collaboration / project team
lead_institutions: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: The paper gives realistic parameters and sensitivity projections for several construction stages, rather than measured final-DarkGEO limits.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
